evals.prompt: I have olive skin, dark brown hair, and dark brown eyes. Gold jewelry looks better on me. What colors should I wear?
evals.expected_output: Analyzes across all three color dimensions (temperature, value, chroma) plus contrast rather than temperature alone. Notes the gold-jewelry signal suggests warm or neutral-warm, cross-checked with other tests, and recommends a drape test in daylight to confirm. Suggests a likely direction (e.g., Deep/Warm Autumn range) with example neutrals, signature colors, and colors to keep away from the face, framed as a starting point rather than a rule.
assertions: Covers temperature, value, and chroma, not only warm vs cool
Recommends cross-checking with more than one undertone test, ideally a daylight drape test
Provides specific neutrals and accent colors
Treats seasonal labels as guidance, not a rigid rule

evals.prompt: I'm 5'1" and want my legs to look longer. I love wide-leg trousers. How should I style them?
evals.expected_output: Keeps the wide-leg trousers the client loves and styles for leg length using proportion principles: high rise, tucked or cropped top for a 1/3:2/3 split, hem that grazes the floor over a heel/platform or pointed toe, monochrome or tonal column, shoe matched to trouser, vertical lines, and scaled accessories. Uses neutral, non-judgemental language.
assertions: Does not tell the client to abandon wide-leg trousers
Applies the rule of thirds / high-rise with tucked or cropped top
Addresses hem length and shoe choice
Mentions monochrome, tonal, or vertical-line techniques
Uses neutral language about the body

evals.prompt: Style a 6-look e-commerce lookbook for our spring linen collection in sand, olive, and terracotta.
evals.expected_output: Builds a cohesive color story using the given palette with a 60-30-10 or neutral-plus-accent logic, shows complete outfits that cross-sell, varies silhouettes for volume balance, recommends diverse models and checks colors against different skin tones, and gives consistent styling language (shoes, accessories, hair) across all six looks.
assertions: Each of the 6 looks lists specific pieces and colors
Applies a color harmony proportion rule
Keeps a consistent styling language across the lookbook
